To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the lamellar surface is not smooth but rough, that the chain fold surface is not smooth either and that lamellae can fold on themselves, thus creating the complex spherulites observed in crystalline polymers.

the lamellar thickness is determined by the chain folding and the chain length; that the lamellae grow by the attachment of new chains at the lamellar surfaces and by thickening by the addition of new chain folds; and that the spherulite structure is the result of a complex growth process that is controlled by the lamellae and their surface.
the structure of the lamellar and spherulitic architectures is determined by the molecular architecture and that the crystallization kinetics are controlled by nucleation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure of crystalline polymorphs, the structure of crystallites and their interfaces, and the crystallization processes of polymers.
the structure and morphology at the molecular level of crystalline polymethylene and its derivatives.
the study of crystalline polymorphisms, the structure of lamellae and spherulites, and the mechanisms of nucleation and crystal growth.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

electron microscopy is a major tool in the study of the structure and properties of polymers and that it is the most direct and the most powerful tool for understanding the molecular structure and properties of crystalline polymery.

electron microscopy is an essential tool for the analysis of the morphology and structure of crystalline polymethylenes and related polymers, in particular in relation to their crystallization processes and properties.
the electron microscope is an indispensable tool in the analysis of the structure and properties of crystalline polymorphs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the electron microscope is a very powerful instrument for the analysis of crystalline polymorphs, their growth and the resulting structures.
electron microscopy imaging and electron diffraction are the only methods that can reach a molecular understanding of the crystalline structure and morphology of polymers.
electron microscopy has been and remains a very fruitful tool to understand the molecular structure of crystalline polymorphs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the morphology of crystalline materials is not random and can be predicted from their structure.

the morphology of crystalline polymer materials is determined by a complex interplay between the molecular architecture, the thermodynamics of crystallization and the kinetics of crystallite growth and aggregation.
electron microscopy, and in particular electron microscopy of polymers, is a powerful tool for understanding the molecular and supramolecular structure of materials.
